subject: Private deployment: operator access, BYOK, and subprocessor evidence request
messages:
From: Anne Keller <anne.keller@cedarhealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cedarhealth.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment - evidence & KMS responsibilities

Hi Sofia / Priya,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — CedarHealth is interested in the Private Deployment option but our procurement and security teams need a handful of confirmations before we can proceed to legal. Can you provide the following: 

- A clear statement of whether Redwood operators have any ability to access tenant plaintext when the customer provides/controls keys (BYOK). We need language we can put in our vendor review.
- A list of subprocessors (current and planned) that would have any role in operating Private deployments, including cloud partners, monitoring vendors, and any on-call/forensics vendors.
- Evidence artifacts: SOC2 report (redacted okay), an operator access playbook or break-glass procedure, and an architecture diagram showing data flow for the VPC/on-prem package.
- Any constraints on regions / cross-border transfer when using Redwood Private (we host collector endpoints during upgrades, not comfortable with uncontrolled egress).

I've attached our vendor questionnaire (CedarHealth_VendorQuestionnaire_v1.pdf) — please put answers inline or point me to a bundle. Procurement would also like to confirm that Redwood will not require key escrow for a production deployment.

Can you confirm an ETA for the package? We usually need this within 5 business days for our procurement window.

Best,
Anne Keller
Sr. Manager, Vendor Risk & Compliance
CedarHealth

Attachment: CedarHealth_VendorQuestionnaire_v1.pdf

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment - evidence & KMS responsibilities

Neha / Priya — forwarding CedarHealth's ask below. Short summary of what we should provide and draft positions: 

1) BYOK and operator access: we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) where keys are held in the customer's cloud KMS and never persist in plaintext on our side. Operators do not have default access to tenant plaintext. We do have a documented break-glass procedure for emergency recovery (time-limited, audited).

2) Subprocessors: we maintain a list; for Private deployments it is smaller (e.g., monitoring, on-call provider, limited cloud infra partners). We'll provide current and planned list and explain roles.

3) Evidence bundle: SOC2 (we can provide a redacted report), operator-access-playbook (internal), and an architecture diagram. We may need legal signoff on what we can share in the playbook.

4) Key escrow: Cedar is explicit they don't accept escrow. We must confirm whether we can fully support non-escrow BYOK for their pattern (VPC + optional on-prem control plane).

Proposed next steps: Neha to craft a short \"operator no-access except break-glass\" paragraph and a subprocessor disclosure CSV; Priya to produce the architecture/dataflow diagram and note cross-border constraints. I can assemble the evidence bundle and propose a 30-min call with Anne to walk through.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

Sofia — thanks, here's a draft legal/security response we can use in the bundle and in a DPA redline: 

- Operator access: "Redwood Inference personnel shall not access or attempt to access customer plaintext data or customer-managed encryption keys during normal operations when the customer has enabled BYOK. Operator access to plaintext or customer keys is permitted only under a documented break-glass process that requires dual-approval from Redwood's Security Lead and the customer's designated approver, is time-limited, fully logged, and is used solely for service restoration. All such events will be reported in accordance with the DPA."

- Subprocessor disclosure: we will provide a current list and commit to 30 days' notice for additions that materially affect data handling. For Private deployments we can limit the disclosed set to: cloud infra partner (if used for bursts), monitoring vendor, and vendor X for on-call. We'll include roles and SOC status in the CSV.

- Evidence: we can share a redacted SOC2 report, our operator-access playbook (section redacted for internal contact info), and an architecture diagram showing data egress controls. For Cedar's no-escrow requirement: confirm that our BYOK path (customer KMS + no key material held by Redwood) is supported end-to-end. We should explicitly state that we do not require key escrow for this configuration.

I'll attach a short playbook extract and the subprocessor CSV to this thread for Sofia to include. Priya: can you confirm the exact regions we plan to use for Cedar (they're US-only per initial call)? If so, call out in the diagram and provide any geo-fence assurances.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: operator-access-playbook.pdf, subprocessor-disclosure.csv

From: Anne Keller <anne.keller@cedarhealth.com>

Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -07:00

Neha / Sofia — thank you, this is the level of detail we need. A couple of clarifying Qs: 

- Break-glass: can you confirm the maximum time window for remedial access (e.g., 1 hour, 4 hours)? We need a SLA for restoration and the maximum duration an operator session could remain active.
- Proof of auditability: does the access logging include the impacted tenant id and a full RPC trace? We will want that as evidence.
- Regions: Cedar requires US-only hosting for PHI. We need a written confirmation that the Private deployment and any temporary artifacts will not leave US regions. Does Redwood plan to use any international support vendors that might need to access logs?

Also — we cannot accept any form of key escrow where Redwood or a third party has ability to reconstruct keys. That must be customer-only. If that is your supported posture we can proceed.

Can you share a redlined DPA or a short statement we can attach to our risk review? Procurement has asked for the package by EOB next Wednesday (2026-09-09).

Thanks,
Anne

Anne — thanks for the follow-ups. Short answers and next steps below: 

- Break-glass window: our policy caps operator remedial sessions to a maximum of 2 hours without reauthorization; initial access is limited to 15 minutes to diagnose and then must be renewed by dual-approval. We'll include this SLA text in the evidence bundle.

- Auditability: all break-glass events include tenant id, full request/response RPC traces where available, and per-request metadata (operator id, timestamps, justification). Logs are immutable and retained per our retention schedule; we'll include a sample log extract in the bundle.

- Regions and cross-border: for CedarHealth we will confirm US-only for deployment artifacts and operational support. Any support vendors that would require cross-border access must be explicitly disclosed; currently we do not plan to engage international support for Cedar. We'll include a statement of US-only operations in the DPA redline.

- Key escrow: confirmed — Redwood will not require or hold key escrow for this deployment. BYOK will be customer-managed; Redwood will not store key material that could reconstruct customer keys. 

Attached: evidence-bundle.zip (contains redacted SOC2, architecture diagram, playbook excerpt, subprocessor CSV). I'll follow up with a short DPA redline and propose a 30-min meeting early next week to walk through the bundle. Proposed times: Mon 9/6 10:00-10:30 PT or Tue 9/7 11:00-11:30 PT — please pick one and we'll send an invite.

Regards,
